claims.claim: Scrap power banks for sale in Ibadan.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show two black cylindrical plastic items with side ports and a blue-green cable connected; no readable power bank branding/labels, and the form factor/ports do not clearly match typical power banks.

risks.risk: Item identity mismatch: the cylinders may be a different electrical device/part (e.g., pump/blower component, battery pack housing, or other equipment) rather than power banks.
risks.proof: A clear close-up of any label/marking/model/brand and the full device setup showing what the cylinders connect to and what they do.
risks.if_unproven: Price as scrap/unknown electrical items with no confirmed function.

risks.risk: Not working / dead cells: even if they are battery-related, they may not hold charge or may be unsafe.
risks.proof: A clip showing power-on/charging behavior (e.g., indicator lights, voltage reading, or a working load test) and the cable/connector end intact.
risks.if_unproven: Price as non-working scrap (no guaranteed charge capacity).

risks.risk: Safety hazard: damaged or leaking batteries, short risk, or missing protective casing/insulation.
risks.proof: Close-up inspection of the ends/ports and any swelling, corrosion, burn marks, or exposed wiring; plus a photo of the connector area and any seals.
risks.if_unproven: Price at the lowest scrap level due to potential battery hazard.

risks.risk: Incomplete units: missing covers, filters, attachments, or internal components (ports suggest parts may be exposed).
risks.proof: Photos showing the full circumference and both ends of each cylinder, including any missing caps/attachments, and what accessories are included.

risks.risk: Unknown specifications: voltage/capacity/ratings not visible; cannot confirm compatibility or value.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the rating plate/spec sticker (voltage, capacity mAh/Wh, model) and any certification markings.

proof_requests: Send clear close-up photos of any label/brand/model/rating on each cylinder (both ends and the side band/label).
Show the full setup: what the blue-green cable connects to, and what the device does when powered/charged.
Provide a working test clip (indicator lights/charging response) and, if possible, a voltage/capacity reading.
Show the connector end-to-end (no cut wires) and confirm there is no swelling, leakage, corrosion, or burn damage.
Confirm completeness: photos of all parts/covers/attachments included and whether any pieces are missing.
response.reason: The witness can only confirm the physical appearance (two worn black cylindrical units with ports and a connected cable) but not that they are power banks or working. A worst-case scrap/unknown-electrical valuation is appropriate until labels and a test prove otherwise.
